column3: AeroGuard on Cardano: agents pay per request for flight outcomes any contract can verify.

The agent asks our server. It answers 402: pay in tADA. The wallet signs a Cardano transaction, the facilitator puts it on chain, and the agent gets the verdict plus the Airnode's signature, which any contract can check.

This is a real run on Cardano preprod. Preflight checks the keys and the balance. The server asks for two tADA. The wallet signs, but never broadcasts; the facilitator does. After one block, about forty seconds, sped up here, we get the verdict for flight IB1314: arrived, signed by the AeroDataBox Airnode. The transaction hash is our receipt.
What the agent gets back: the verdict, landed twenty-five minutes early. The proof, the Airnode's signature over exactly this data. And the receipt, the Cardano payment that bought it.
Two tADA for one verdict. No account, no API key. You can check it on Cardanoscan.
Our dashboard shows the same exchange in three steps: the 402 offer, the payment, and the signed verdict.

And it's not just JSON. Our Aiken escrow on Cardano checks the same Airnode signature with Plutus builtins, so the cover pays only on a signed result. Forged data fails, real landings pass: forty-four tests out of forty-four.
Last night our first four policies landed. The same signed answers closed them on Base, and settle the Cardano contract exactly the same way. One signature, one verdict, two chains.
Cardano can also pay for the insurance itself: the premium in tADA buys a policy on Base, and the policy records the Cardano payment.
Agents pay per request on Cardano, for flight outcomes any contract can verify.
